title: The 3-Tier Web App
summary: Turn a static site into a real application with a load-balanced app tier and a database.
narrative:
Your portfolio grew into a product. It has accounts, a dashboard, and data that changes — this is no longer a bundle of files a CDN can just cache. You need to compute responses and store state.

The canonical answer is the three-tier architecture: a load balancer spreads traffic across a fleet of stateless web servers, and those servers read and write a shared database. Done right, you can add servers to handle more users and survive the loss of any single one.

Build the classic pattern — client, load balancer, redundant app tier, and a database — and keep the client well away from the data tier. A cache in front of the database is the finishing touch.

functional: Persist application state in a database
Spread traffic across multiple app servers
nonFunctional: No single server failure takes the app offline
constraints: Clients enter through the load balancer only
Only the app tier may talk to the database
capacity: Millions of rows in the database
specs.tradeoff: A stateless app tier trades local session convenience for the freedom to scale horizontally and fail over.
specs.bonus: Add a Cache in front of the database to absorb repeated reads.

missions.label: Send Client traffic to the Load Balancer
Balance across the Web Server tier
Let the app tier read/write the Database
Cache hot reads from the app tier

topologyRules.message: Traffic must enter through the Load Balancer, not straight to a Web Server.
Clients must never talk to the database directly.
Database access must go through the application tier.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers behind the Load Balancer so a single failure isn't an outage.

hints: The load balancer is the front door. Wire Client → Load Balancer → Web Server.
Add a second Web Server and connect the Load Balancer to both — that's how you kill the single point of failure.
Only the Web Server should reach the SQL Database. A Cache between them soaks up repeated reads.
